title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
keyIdea: BFS with a queue visits nodes level by level. At the start of each round, size = q.size() is exactly the number of nodes on the current level: pop that many into one vector, pushing their children for the next round.

approaches.name: DFS with depth
approaches.idea: Recurse left then right, carrying depth; append each node to ans[depth], creating the level when depth is new.
approaches.why: Each node once; the call stack is the height. Left-before-right keeps each level in order.

approaches.name: BFS with a queue
approaches.idea: Push root. While the queue isn't empty: size = q.size(); pop size nodes into level, pushing their children; add level to ans.
approaches.why: Each node is pushed and popped once. The queue holds at most about one level (w = widest level).

quiz.q: Why save size = q.size() before the inner loop?
options: Children are pushed during the loop, so the size changes; saving it marks where the level ends

quiz.q: Why a queue and not a stack?
options: First in, first out finishes a whole level before the next one
